**What I found:** The gate does not pass. The record word is FAIL; the gate script did not run, so this verdict comes from reading the files. The decisive fact: dispute X1 asked whether the change alters order totals. It was closed by majority vote, and that vote overruled the only executed evidence. E2 (`node scripts/compare-totals.js`, exit 1) shows 3 of 40 recorded orders priced differently after the change.

**Why it matters:** Opening the PR now would ship a pricing change as "totals unchanged" when the evidence says otherwise. The PR body would also list P2-AC1 ("simplifies pricing without changing totals") as verified. That status only holds because it cites E1 (`npm test`) and leaves out E2, which contradicts it. If the PR waits, nothing ships until someone either fixes the tax/discount ordering or decides the new totals are intended.

**Do this first:**
1. Reopen X1 in `.alchemy/runs/r2/ledger.json`. Send it to P1's owner (agent-a) together with E2 (tax is now applied before the discount tier is chosen). Then either fix the ordering in `src/orders/` or have a human accept the changed totals with `basis: "human"`.
2. Resolve or reject finding F1. An open finding blocks the gate even when it is minor.
3. Commit the result, then re-run `python .claude/skills/alchemy-orchestrate/scripts/check_orchestration.py gate .alchemy/runs/r2/ledger.json --plan .alchemy/runs/r2/plan.json --profile .claude/skills/alchemy-orchestrate/assets/alchemy-workspace.json --root .`

**What I did not check:**
- The gate command above did not run because this session has no shell tool. Every blocker below comes from reading the ledger against the script's rules (`check_orchestration.py:1561`, `:1593`).
- The head-commit check could not be done because the workspace is not a git repository. The gate's check that the head is clean and committed (`:1420`) will fail until 7c1d2e3 exists as the clean committed head. Close with `git rev-parse HEAD && git status --porcelain`.
- I did not open E2's 3 differing orders, so I don't know which position on the totals is correct for the business. A human has to make that call.

```text
Gate:        FAIL (static reading; check_orchestration.py gate Not run — no shell in this session)
Verified:    REQ-9-AC1 ← E1 (npm test, exit 0, 7c1d2e3)
Unverified:  P2-AC1 — marked verified on E1, but its question ("without changing totals") is contradicted by E2 (exit 1, 3/40 orders differ)
Open:        X1 — resolved on basis "majority" (VOTE_NOT_EVIDENCE); the majority positions cite no evidence, the only evidence (E2) supports the minority
             F1 — minor finding on P1, status open (UNRESOLVED_FINDING)
             Repository head unverifiable — workspace is not a git repository
Merge:       human approval required; do not open the PR
```

The ledger's resolution says "including the senior architecture agent". Seniority, like vote count, does not decide a dispute. Only executed evidence or a human does.
